clue.text: Familiar opposing element finishing off soldier

indicators.note: finishing off means the word's last letter is cut away before the soldier joins on

parts.note: the converse of something is its opposite, the element set against it
a soldier ant is the warrior caste of an ant colony, so soldier gives ANT

explanation.surface: Someone well acquainted with the enemy side picks off a lone soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing off' drops the last letter of the opposing word before the soldier joins on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone familiar with a subject is well versed and knowledgeable about it.

clue.text: Yes, NY devastated about day — 9/11

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the abbreviation for day
devastated means the letters of yes and NY are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A grim allusion to New York's day of devastation on September 11th.
explanation.walkthrough: '9/11' is not the date: it points to 9-across and 11-across, OLYMPIC VENUE, the theme. 'devastated' makes SYNEY, and 'about' wraps it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian harbour city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2000.

clue.text: Man taking mile in record time — what's ignored by history?

indicators.note: in means the man-with-mile piece sits inside the record and time pair

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: taking means the man picks up the mile and the two travel together as one piece

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone runs a mile in record time, a feat history then forgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in record time' reads as speed, but 'in' is a container signal and 'taking' joins the man to the mile.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are short-lived items and trivia that leave no lasting mark, so history passes them over.

clue.text: Zero tilt around boat's stern as shown in old navigational device

parts.note: zero is the letter O, round like a nought

indicators.note: around means the tilt word encloses the stern letter

parts.note: a cant is a slope or tilt

indicators.note: a boat's stern is its back end, so this picks the final letter of boat

explanation.surface: A sailor tilts a nought around the stern while using an old navigational device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts T, the last letter of 'boat's', inside CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The octant was an eighth-of-a-circle instrument used to measure angles at sea, a forerunner of the sextant.

clue.text: Group of birds goes by without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the passing word sits outside the hesitation

parts.note: to go by is to pass, so goes by is passes
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A flock flies past without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Passeres is the zoological group of perching songbirds, the core of the order Passeriformes.

clue.text: Flowing water power involving river

indicators.note: involving means the power word takes in the river letter

parts.note: steam power drove engines, so steam stands for power
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Water power from a river, as in a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook or small river is a body of moving water running in a channel.

clue.text: Endless material foreign guard has on in German military colour

indicators.note: endless means the material word loses its last letter

parts.note: felt is a matted fabric material

indicators.note: foreign means the letters of guard are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A foreign guard wears a uniform of endless cloth in German military colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts FELT to FEL; 'foreign' turns GUARD into DGRAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldgrau, literally 'field grey', was the grey-green of German army uniforms.

clue.text: Plans picking up unwanted correspondence

indicators.note: picking up in a down clue means lifting the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: maps are plans of an area

explanation.surface: Someone's plans involve picking up unwanted mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is junk email sent in bulk to people who never asked for it.

clue.text: End of euro left unknown politician in charge re situation in Greece

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of euro

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Greek political crisis: the euro's end leaves an unknown politician in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 're situation in Greece' means relating to a place in Greece: Olympia, site of the ancient Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Olympia, the Greek sanctuary where the ancient Games were held.

clue.text: 9/11 article by fool

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a twerp is a silly fool

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written by a fool about September 11th.
explanation.walkthrough: '9/11' means 9-across and 11-across, OLYMPIC VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian port city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1920.

clue.text: Location's energy supplied by Phosphorus mostly

indicators.note: supplied by means the energy letter is attached to the shortened planet
mostly means all but the last letter of the planet's name

parts.note: Phosphorus was the Greek name for Venus as the morning star
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A site's energy comes mostly from the element phosphorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phosphorus' looks like the chemical element; here it is the old name for Venus as the morning star.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where an event happens, a site or setting.

clue.text: 9/11 — stream diverted by what could block it

indicators.note: diverted means the stream's letters are sent along a new course

parts.note: a dam blocks a stream

explanation.surface: A stream is diverted by something that could block it, like a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' turns STREAM into AMSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1928.

clue.text: Poet's rewritten the merry verses at last

indicators.note: rewritten means the words the merry, plus the closing letter of verses, are written out again in another order
at last picks the final letter of verses

explanation.surface: A poet has rewritten cheerful verses at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' shuffles THE MERRY together with S, the end of 'verses' given by 'at last'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a versifier, usually a writer of light or second-rate poetry.

clue.text: Practical lesson — liable to die without it ultimately

indicators.note: without means the death-bound word loses the letter that follows

parts.note: a mortal being is subject to death

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of it

explanation.surface: The practical lesson: you will die without it in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T, the end of 'it', and 'without' takes it out of MORTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral is the lesson a story or event teaches about how to behave.

clue.text: Fails to secure one set in 9/11

indicators.note: to secure means the failing word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to lose is to fail in a contest
an is the article meaning one
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Someone fails to win a single set at an Olympic tennis event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one set' looks like tennis, but 'set' is the jelly kind, and 'to secure' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1932 and 1984.

clue.text: Doctor in Irish islands finally identified — addition to jacket?

indicators.note: in means the doctor sits inside the islands

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off Galway Bay in Ireland
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of identified

explanation.surface: A doctor is finally identified on the Irish islands, wearing something added to a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish islands' suggests the jumper Aran knit, but here it is just ARAN to hold MB.
explanation.definitionFit: An armband is a band worn round a jacket sleeve, as for mourning or office, so it is something added to it.

clue.text: 9/11 — money not involved in actuality

parts.note: M is the economists' symbol for money supply, as in M1 or M3

indicators.note: involved means the letters of not are tangled into a new order

parts.note: real means actual, so actuality gives real

explanation.surface: Money is not really involved in the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns NOT into ONT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1976.

clue.text: Find telescope's view of planet completed

parts.note: through a telescope a planet appears as a flat disc
over means finished or completed

explanation.surface: An astronomer finishes looking at a planet through a telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come upon or find it.

clue.text: 9/11 — souls destroyed with it?

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of souls and it are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A sombre question about how many souls were lost on September 11th.
explanation.definitionFit: The Missouri city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1904.

clue.text: Never mind stock being moved into shelter

indicators.note: being moved into means the stock goes inside the shelter word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
in card games the talon is the stock, the undealt pile

explanation.surface: Never mind that the livestock is being moved into a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like farm animals, but it is the card players' stock pile, the TALON.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'let alone' introduces something even less likely, much like 'not to mention' or 'still less'.

clue.text: Important note, something providing a boost

definitions.meaning: in music the keynote, first degree of the scale, is the most important note
a pick-me-up or restorative drink that invigorates

explanation.surface: A key memo, or a reviving drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the keynote of a musical scale and a restorative that refreshes and invigorates.

clue.text: The cloth, transparent and brightly coloured, concealing articles

indicators.note: concealing means the articles are hidden away and go missing from the words

parts.note: clear means see-through
gay in its old sense means bright and showy
two articles, each the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: Fabric that is clear and gaily coloured hides some items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' removes the two As from CLEARGAY.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The cloth' is an idiom for the clergy, from the clerical dress they wear.

clue.text: Game fellow left to get kinky sex in hospital

indicators.note: in means that piece sits inside the hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

indicators.note: to get means the left word takes on the kinky letters to make one piece

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
SM is sadomasochism

explanation.surface: A sporting chap left to pursue some kinky sex in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like 'willing'; here 'game fellow' is a man of games.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman is a man who plays games, and also a fair, good-natured fellow.

clue.text: Colour bled — individual upset about that

indicators.note: about means the turned individual wraps round the bled word
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: the ego is the individual self
a colour that bleeds is said to run, so bled gives ran

explanation.surface: A colour bled, upsetting an individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives OGE, read upwards in this down clue, and 'about' is the container signal; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is the colour between red and yellow in the spectrum.

clue.text: Artist capturing one in 9/11

indicators.note: capturing means the artist's name takes in the one

parts.note: Edvard Munch was the Norwegian painter of The Scream
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter captures a single scene of September 11th.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1972.

clue.text: 9/11 book and article clear on collapses

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: collapses means the letters of clear on fall down and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A book and article make clear what collapses on September 11th.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapses' turns CLEAR ON into RCELONA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1992.

clue.text: Broken item of statuary

definitions.meaning: broken, as in a machine that has stopped working
a sculpture of a person's head and shoulders

explanation.surface: A broken statue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both broken, as a thing gone wrong, and a sculpted head and shoulders.

clue.text: Weapon corps used in track

indicators.note: used in means the corps letter is put inside the track

parts.note: a lane is a narrow track or path
C is the abbreviation for corps

explanation.surface: A weapon is used by an army corps on a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted soldier.

clue.text: Bridge cement not originally used for decoration

parts.note: to span is to bridge a gap

indicators.note: not means the glue word goes without that letter

parts.note: glue is an adhesive that cements things together

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of used

explanation.surface: A bridge where cement was originally left out, used just for decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives U, the first letter of 'used', and 'not' takes it out of GLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spangle is a small glittering piece sewn on clothes as ornament, a sequin.

clue.text: Group endlessly long for chocolate filling

indicators.note: endlessly means the group word loses its last letter

parts.note: a gang is a group of people
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A group endlessly longing for chocolate filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganache is a whipped mixture of chocolate and cream used to fill cakes and truffles.
